preamble: The change of the lateral approximant [l] to the voiced dental fricative [ð] is rare. Its clearest attestation is in Woods Cree, where Proto-Algonquian *l surfaces as ð (written th). This reflex is one of the main isoglosses dividing the Cree dialect continuum into y-, n-, l-, r- and ð-dialects. The Proto-Algonquian liquid is written *l following Bloomfield; Goddard argues it was a rhotic *r, so the exact value of the source sound is not certain.

examples.note: cf. Plains Cree kīya, Swampy Cree kīna, Moose Cree kīla

sources: Bloomfield, L. (1946). Algonquian. In H. Hoijer (Ed.), Linguistic Structures of Native America. Viking Fund Publications in Anthropology 6.
